hints.title: Recursive Subtree Depth Aggregation
hints.text: The maximum depth of an arbitrary tree equals one plus the highest depth among all of its children nodes.

hints.title: Base Case and Branch Traversal
hints.text: If the root is NULL, return 0. If children is empty, return 1. Otherwise, recursively compute the depth of every child and pick the maximum.

hints.title: Depth Function Blueprint
hints.text: Define maxDepth(root): if not root, return 0. If not root.children, return 1. Return 1 + max(maxDepth(c) for c in root.children).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: total number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Every node is visited once during recursive traversal with call frame height bounded by H.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-traversing children from top to bottom repeatedly causes redundant quadratic inspections.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Depth recursion uses implicit call frame memory proportional to tree depth.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling NULL roots and nodes with zero children cleanly without extra branches.
